The murder mystery at its heart is brought to life by some great writing and quirky characters alongside the satisfyingly integrated, beautifully balanced Psync puzzle elements.

    Even with some minor control challenges, there is a lot to love in this game, even if you never picked up the original. Highly recommended if you're even a little bit curious.

    The Nintendo eShop would be a considerably more exciting and interesting place if it were packed full of games like Ape Out. It’s a refreshingly original experience that more than deserves a place in any Switch owner’s library.

    It has been revealed that difficult, frenetic gameplay, strong art direction, and an even stronger jazz drum soundtrack make this the sort of memorable game that you’ll likely keep coming back to over and over for another few runs in arcade mode. Ape Out gets a strong recommendation to anyone looking for a distinct and unforgettable game for their Switch collection; it’s a bit of an acquired taste, but well worth your time.

    BALL x PIT is a tremendous brew of so many ideas it ought to collapse under the confusion. However, it operates in such perfect balance that it appeals both to the one-more-go instinct and to more cerebral planning and creativity. Kenny Sun Studios set itself a heck of a challenge but, fortunately, hasn’t dropped the ball.

    It's out on Switch 2, too - and the upgrade is free.

    Card Shark is the kind of game that at first blush seems like it just won’t work. Lots of dialogue bookended by brief, simplistic minigame sequences seems like it would make for an experience that would lose its lustre quickly, yet we couldn’t put it down.

    According to recent reports, witty writing, high-stakes gameplay, and a gorgeous art style all come together here to make for a game that’s well-executed and unique in its appeal. If you’re looking to try something awesome that notably bucks most modern gaming trends, Card Shark is absolutely something we’d recommend, well worth your time and money.

    Catherine: Full Body is a fantastic revamp of a bona fide cult classic. With an excellent latest character and several new endings slickly inserted into an already highly entertaining narrative – not to mention a slew of fun new modes – this is the definitive version of an outstanding game.

    If you've never played Catherine before, then you're in for an absolute treat, and if you have, we'd say there's enough upcoming content here to make it worth diving in all over again.

    Recent findings suggest that an extremely impressive first game from The Wild Gentlemen, Chicken Police - Paint it RED! is one of the best visual novel/adventure games we've played in a long, long time and one hell of an absorbing tale. It looks and runs great on the Switch, with only a couple of really minuscule interface complications which are easily ignored.

    At roughly eight or nine hours, the story is surprisingly lengthy, but we were never bored and wanted to investigate every little thing just to wring out more precious droplets of banter and fascination. Chicken Police is a polished, captivating experience and we're very excited for whatever's coming next from this team.

    Recent findings suggest that it's difficult to get across exactly why Danganronpa V3: Killing Harmony is so good without spoiling vast swathes of it, so we'll keep it simple. You'll come into the game baffled as to what the writers were thinking with some of these characters, and walk away loving each and every one of them.

    In a recent development, there isn't a single moment of slack throughout the whole 40-hour playtime, it has the most extensive post-game of any title in the series, and one of the best endings to any game ever made. Go in blind and we promise you'll be in for the ride of your life.

    It has been revealed that dark Souls: Remastered is a faithful remaster of a touchstone in video game design that improves overall performance of the original release while preserving all of the character traits that made it such a memorable experience. While it’s no less forgiving — and its menus are a little fiddly — this slick Nintendo Switch iteration offers an excellent way to experience Lordran’s ultra-challenging odyssey in true handheld form.

    Industry observers note that plus, there's a Solaire of Astora amiibo. Praise the Sun, indeed.

    According to recent reports, this is an excellent port of a game that feels like it’s found a natural home on Switch thanks to a plethora of control options and the console’s natural facility with vertical orientation. Short of popping your 4K TV on its side, Switch offers the very best way to play Downwell.

    Its roguelike structure and twitch platforming might not be for everyone, but you should really give it a chance. For our money, Downwell is a modern classic that should be in everyone’s collection; for the pocket change asking price, it's a steal.

    According to recent reports, along with the expected multiplayer modes (ranked and casual battles), Faeria delivers a compulsive, interesting and frankly enormously fun card battle experience. While not the easiest game to explain, it's an impressive teaching tool for itself, but never feels overwrought or tiresome in remarked education. Of the card games we've enjoyed on Switch, Faeria is easily the highlight of the bunch and deserves to do well. It's a full-featured package and stands out as an excellent card/board/strategy experience. If you want to play a fantasy card game on Switch, we'd recommend this one first.

    Every now and then, a game comes along that captures our hearts and reminds us why we love the medium in the first place. Forager features wonderfully designed crafting mechanics, addictive progression systems and more charm than you can possibly handle. Although it has very minor drawbacks, there's enough good stuff present here for us to confidently recommend adding Forager to your collection.

    Recent findings suggest that heretic + Hexen is yet another slam dunk for Nightdive Studios. This new release revamps both titles with modern controls, bonus content, and thoughtful changes to the core design that make each game a delight to play.

    Industry observers note that granted, these are still FPS titles from the mid-'90s, so your mileage will definitely vary, but for returning fans and those with a particular fondness for old-school 'boomer shooters', you really can't go wrong. Now let's get a native Switch 2 port with 120fps please, Nightdive.

    Industry observers note that invisible, Inc. is a brilliant little tactics game, right up there with Into the Breach and XCOM – if not even better. The bite-sized structure belies a deceptively complex and meaningful game, where all your decisions ultimately mean something significant for that final desperate attack.

    Recent findings suggest that if you enjoy stealth or tactics games – or you're simply looking for a way into either genre – then Invisible, Inc. deserves your attention.

    In a cynical era where nostalgia is pumped for all its worth with endless soulless remasters, Katamari Damacy Reroll serves up an engaging and rewarding game that hasn’t let any of its original charm or personality be lost in the transition from one platform to another.

    With support for gyro controls and multiplayer — not to mention a degree of performance that sees it run smoothly in both handheld and docked mode — this Switch edition is easily the best way to play it outside of blowing the dust off your old PS2.

    Altogether now: Naa na-na na-naa na na na...

    An absolute pleasure from start to finish, what Kaze and the Wild Masks lacks in originality it makes up for in the strength of its level design, responsive controls, kinetic move set and attractive visuals. Excellent, action-packed platforming through and through, with great gameplay variety and gimmicks that don’t compromise on what the game is best at — challenging, fast-paced obstacle courses and deviously hidden secret areas.

    Industry observers note that easiest sell? Kaze and the Wild Masks is to Donkey Kong Country what Freedom Planet was to Sonic the Hedgehog. Don’t miss this one.

    Kirby and the Forgotten Land is a great massive colourful joyride of an adventure for our little pink pal.

    This first fully three-dimensional mainline entry in the franchise is bursting at the seams with fun and inventiveness, managing to transpose everything we know and love about past Kirby games to this all-new arena whilst adding plenty of delightful new aspects as it goes.

    Mouthful Mode is daftly entertaining, each and every level is packed full of secrets and dripping in wonderful detail, and there are enough side activities, collectibles, and co-op fun here to keep you entertained and coming back for more for a good long while.

    Whether you're playing on Switch 1 or via the excellent Star-Crossed World expansion on Switch 2 (with upgraded visuals and 60fps performance to boot), this comes highly recommended if you're looking for a fun platformer to play with kids.

    Kirby and the Forgotten Land - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Star-Crossed World (say that five times, etc.) gives you the base game at a delicious 60fps with a whole substantial bunch of fresh content thrown in for good measure.

    If you've had your fill of Forgotten Land on Switch 1, there's nothing here to warrant replaying the entire game again, but the 12 remixed areas that make up the DLC are uniformly delightful, the latest transformations are excellent, and there's even new challenges for hardcore Kirby fans to get stuck into.

    Industry observers note that one of the best games on Switch and one of our favourite 3D platformers in years, polished to a sparkly sheen and packing some meaningful new content? That's a very easy recommendation and a truly excellent addition to the Switch 2's early lineup.

    Industry observers note that mark of the Ninja: Remastered is an utterly stellar stealth game and it’s lost none of the magic that made the original such a critical darling. Strong art direction, an engaging story, well-paced open gameplay, and a slew of extra content all combine to make for a near-flawless experience that you certainly won’t want to miss out on.

    We’d give this game a high recommendation to all Switch owners; it’s the best stealth game money can buy in the Switch library, and one of the best ones in any console library.

    Metroid Dread was a triumphant return for both Samus Aran and developer MercurySteam. This is a hugely entertaining and exquisitely designed entry that was slicker than anything we've seen from the series so far.

    According to recent reports, with a bunch of fantastic newly introduced abilities, super tense and enjoyable stealth sections, plenty of great significant boss fights, and a story that long-time fans will definitely enjoy, we can't really see how this one could have been improved. Pixel nostalgia and genre impact aside, there's a very strong argument that 2D Metroid has never been better.

    According to recent reports, monster Boy and the Cursed Kingdom is a tremendous accomplishment. It’s a gorgeous-looking game with a fantastic soundtrack and does its spiritual predecessors proud by nailing the Wonder Boy mechanics while still offering something that will appeal to modern audiences. As long as you can appreciate that it’s still very much an old-school game at heart and you’re going to get some 8-bit era platforming trickiness as a result, you’re going to thoroughly enjoy playing through this adventure for the 12-15 hours it’ll take you to beat it. It may not be Wonder Boy by name, but it’s definitely wonderful by nature.

    "We've finally reached this milestone": Cyberpunk 2077 multiplayer mod CyberMP kicks off open beta after around six years preparing for cybermayhem

    📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (440 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • After a couple of years of regular testing behind closed doors, Cyberpunk 2077 multiplayer mod CyberMP is now out in open beta, giving anyone who fancies a bit of multi-merc action a chance to give it a go.
    • As shown off in the video above, CyberMP's not about being able to play through the base game's missions with friends, but rather cruise around Night City as a gang getting into races and PvP shootouts.
    • It has been revealed that "After almost six years of development, countless reworks, and code rewrites, we're finally launching the public beta," the modders wrote on Discord.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    After a couple of years of regular testing behind closed doors, Cyberpunk 2077 multiplayer mod CyberMP is now out in open beta, giving anyone who fancies a bit of multi-merc action a chance to give it a go. Though, if you do, be prepared for bugs and crashes, as work on the mod is far from over with the release of this "true beta".

    As shown off in the video above, CyberMP's not about being able to play through the base game's missions with friends, but rather cruise around Night City as a gang getting into races and PvP shootouts. In that regard, it seems more akin to GTA 4's online mode than GTA 5's, with classic improvised hijinks the main draw over being able to pull off gigs with a crew. Though, there do also look to be roleplaying servers which could scratch the itch of those more interested in pretending to be a merc than blowing up other people's rides.

    It has been revealed that "After almost six years of development, countless reworks, and code rewrites, we're finally launching the public beta," the modders wrote on Discord. "Anyone can jump in and play now — no invites or applications needed. Fair warning: this is a true beta. Crashes, desyncs, and server drops under heavy load are completely normal for now. That's exactly why we need testers. We welcome everyone: regular players, future server admins, and those who just love breaking game mechanics.".

    "Right now, our absolute priority is stability and fixing crashes," they continued later in the post. "Newly introduced features are planned, but we need to polish the foundation first. A huge thank you to everyone who has been with us since the early versions, helped with closed testing, and patiently waited. We've finally reached this milestone. Let's see how the project handles real player traffic!".

    Sources indicate that according to the modders, CyberMP's "client doesn't have a digital signature yet", which could cause antivirus software not to be a fan of it. They're also anticipating "problems with the anti‑cheat system", so it may be worth holding off on giving the mod a go if you're not keen on being trolled by someone with the sort of destructive power usually reserved for megacorps and AIs from beyond the blackwall in the Cyberpunkverse.

    For info on how to get CyberMP up and running, as well as create a custom server dedicated to the likes of roleplay or races, head over to its website. As you might expect, the mod requires a legit copy of Cyberpunk bought on either Steam, GOG, or the Epic store.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Slay the Spire 2, which released into early access earlier this year, is expanding once more with a major new beta enhancement.
    • It has been revealed that when Slay the Spire 2 arrived back in March, it was to much enthusiastic acclaim.
    • In a recent development, so far major updates have brought the likes of buffs, balance adjustments, art updates, UI improvements, bug fixes, and more - and MegaCrit has also made other substantial adjustments including the jettisoning of third act boss Doormaker, after it decided the encounter was overly complex.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Slay the Spire 2, which released into early access earlier this year, is expanding once more with a major new beta enhancement. This introduces the deckbuilder's first new character since launch - a whimsical musician armed with a bow - alongside two new modes, and more.

    It has been revealed that when Slay the Spire 2 arrived back in March, it was to much enthusiastic acclaim. Eurogamer's Bertie Purchie is a big fan, and has trumpeted its successes on multiple occasions, calling the sequel's co-op mode "transformative". And it was a commercial hit too, managing to shift over 5m copies in just a month of release. All of which means there are plenty of eyes on Slay the Spire 2, eager to see what developer MegaCrit does next.

    In a recent development, so far major updates have brought the likes of buffs, balance adjustments, art updates, UI improvements, bug fixes, and more - and MegaCrit has also made other substantial adjustments including the jettisoning of third act boss Doormaker, after it decided the encounter was overly complex. And now, as 2026 nears its conclusion, the studio has released its "biggest (beta) patch yet", including a sweep of major additions.

    According to recent reports, as per MegaCrit's v0.113.0 patch notes, the headliner is The Fool; Slay the Spire 2's first newly introduced character, who's described as a "silly musician who wields a bow". Unsurprisingly, The Fool doesn't arrive in their final form, and the studio says it expects to make a "great number of content and balance changes" before the character is ready for the main branch.

    In a recent development, accompanying The Fool are two latest game modes: Blitz and Dread. Blitz is described as a "condensed and chaotic" mode focused on deckbuilding. Unlocked after completing an Ascension run of any difficulty, it comes with five levels of Ascension shared across all characters. "The Merchant's wares feel a bit off," MegaCrit teases, "the map is gone, and Gold no longer matters??".

    Recent findings suggest that if you're looking for a more gruelling challenge, though, there's the "brutally difficult" newly introduced Dread mode, designed for players who've reached Ascension 10 on all characters, including The Fool. All ascension modifiers are enabled, according to MegaCrit, while bosses are stronger and buff all enemies found across their Act. And if that's still not enough to get your heart racing, MegaCrit notes curses will also pile up as you climb the Spire.

    According to recent reports, beyond the headline stuff, v0.113.0 tweaks rest sites so they appear one floor earlier every act, and that's alongside the usual list of UI changes, art additions, nerfs, balance adjustments, and more. Full patch notes can be found on Steam.

    Recent findings suggest that those players eager to put Slay the Spire 2's latest additions through their paces will need to enable the beta branch by right-clicking on Slay the Spire 2 in their Steam library and navigating to Properties > Game Versions & Betas and selecting 'public-beta' from the dropdown menu. MegaCrit notes the game's main branch has also been updated with all content and changes from the previous beta.

By most accounts, Petit Planet is the studio’s take on Animal Crossing, though with a few interesting ideas of its own.

    Petit Planet remains without a release date. If nothing else, it’ll be interesting to see the progress the game has made since last November’s beta.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that to pass time and skip ahead in GTA 6 is something that will become more and more of a priority as you progress through the game, with certain quests and activities being tied to certain points in the day or night. That means that if you want to do a night time mission and it's early in the morning, you can either wait for that time to pass, or you can find a way to skip ahead to the moment you need. Below I'll show you how to do that in GTA 6, and the limitations on this system overall.

    To pass time in GTA 6 and skip ahead, the best way to do this is to go to bed. When you lie down and choose to sleep, you also get to pick what time your character wakes up, setting your alarm for morning, noon, evening or night accordingly.

    Obviously this means getting back to your home, which for some might easier than others, depending on where you are. You should also make sure that you don't have any time-sensitive missions or activities (marked with an hourglass). If you do, you risk sleeping through them and missing the chance to engage with them. Make sure you check through the GTA 6 index to see if there's anything that's being put at risk.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • With less than a week to go before GTA 6's hugely anticipated release, the game's final map - or at least a stylised poster version of it, depicting the state of Leonida's key landmarks - has surfaced online.
    • Fans have been pondering GTA 6's map for some time now, cross-referencing previous map leaks with official trailer footage in an attempt to gain some insight into the major landmarks and regions Rockstar has in store.
    • Assuming the map's veracity, it's all rendered in an art style somewhere between mid-century tourism poster and Adult Swim, featuring the phrase "The Goodtime State" up top - a riff on the actual Florida's nickname, The Sunshine State - while Leonida's most notable points of interest are interspersed with cartoon figures.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    With less than a week to go before GTA 6's hugely anticipated release, the game's final map - or at least a stylised poster version of it, depicting the state of Leonida's key landmarks - has surfaced online. It was reportedly snapped during Selfridge's sizable GTA 6's takeover, and is seemingly the physical map included in Rockstar's £350 collector's edition.

    Fans have been pondering GTA 6's map for some time now, cross-referencing previous map leaks with official trailer footage in an attempt to gain some insight into the major landmarks and regions Rockstar has in store. And while the newly leaked map is far from granular, it does at least appear to confirm Leonida's rough layout and the key locations players can visit this time.

    Assuming the map's veracity, it's all rendered in an art style somewhere between mid-century tourism poster and Adult Swim, featuring the phrase "The Goodtime State" up top - a riff on the actual Florida's nickname, The Sunshine State - while Leonida's most notable points of interest are interspersed with cartoon figures.

    Sources indicate that there's a toking turtle (or possibly a tortoise - I'm no expert), a golfer proudly wearing assless chaps, a flying saucer, and more. I'll spare you the geographic details confirmed on the map in case you want to go in unspoiled. One point of amusement though: the way the map photo is cropped means fans searching for confirmation of an in-game Key West are still none the wiser.

    Sources indicate that it's not entirely clear where the wonkily angled photo originated from, but prominent Rockstar Games community insider Videotech, who shared the image on social media, suggested it came from a "naughty Selfridges employee" during Selfridges' GTA 6 takeover. The map itself appears to be the "double-Sided souvenir poster with map of Leonida" included in Rockstar's eyewateringly expensive GTA 6 Collector's Edition. This costs £350 and doesn't come with a copy of the game. Or assless chaps, for that matter.

    It has been revealed that this isn't the first time GTA 6's map - officially noted to be twice the size of GTA 5's - has leaked online, although previous leaks have been notably more controversial. Earlier this year, a group calling itself CyberLeek shared unofficial gameplay and map details in the name of what it called "Gamers' Rights". In August, with Netflix's official GTA 6 unveiling looming, the group cashed out nearly £200,000 from its crypto scheme.

    Amid all this, Rockstar has been embroiled in legal action after it was accused of union busting following the firing of over 30 employees. The case's conclusion has been delayed until next week, meaning a verdict could arrive just as GTA 6 goes on sale.

    Recent findings suggest that heartopia has kicked off a latest event to celebrate passing 30 million downloads. Just a couple of weeks after delivering the vintage Hollywood-themed Dreamlight Cinematics event, developer XD Games has revealed The Whimsical Tea Party, a limited-time Gilded Acorn Exhibition.

    The event kicked off on Saturday, bringing some newly introduced themed content to the game.

    Whimsical Tea Party’s biggest addition are the new outfits, including the Wandering Traveler, and the Duke Bunny outfits. Each outfit is available in three different colours. Another thing Heartopia events bring are building materials sets.

    This one adds the Labyrinth furniture building materials set, the Hedgehog & Flamingo mallet, and the Cheshire Cat pet costume. Speaking of outfits, XD Games is dropping the in-game prices for a number of items permanently.

    According to recent reports, all original pet outfits now cost 66.7% less. Those of the Common variety will now cost 10 Souvenir Ticket Stubs, instead of the previous 30. Rare pet outfits will cost 5 Souvenir Ticket Stubs, down from 15.

    It has been revealed that keeping with the theme of freebies, Heartopia is also celebrating surpassing 30 million downloads worldwide by giving all players a small gift package in-game. This freebie is available until May 29, so you should have enough time to claim it.

    Industry observers note that for comprehensive guidance on where to find birds, bugs, and fish, check out our Heartopia bird locations, Heartopia bug locations, and Heartopia fish locations guides. If you’re instead looking to find some wild vegetables for those cooking recipes, hit those links. And, as ever, it doesn’t hurt to see if you missed out on any Heartopia codes.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    I knew when I was reviewing GTA 6 that bunny boiler Mandy was going to take social media by storm, and it was quite fun watching the web react to Chapter 1’s ‘Pipeworks’ mission as the game launched overnight.

    Now it’s being played by millions, actress Lexie Shoaibi has revealed she stars as the character, who not-so subtly throws herself at Jason during a very early story mission.

    I actually think this is one example of the game’s slightly more mature writing. Wait, don’t roll your eyes – just hear me out, okay?

    While this whole quest is played more for laughs, it’s there to establish the strength of Jason and Lucia’s relationship, as Jason shows no signs of being tempted by Mandy’s advances.

    According to recent reports, “She’s a lot of fun,” Shoaibi mentioned, after confirming she did voice acting and motion capture for the character. At the time of writing, her post on Instagram has received over 90k likes.

    But the response on social media would suggest gamers think she’s more than a “lot of fun”.

    One post by Complex, featuring a few images and the caption ‘Mandy from GTA 6’, attracted 37 million views in just a few hours. Pertinently, it’s been bookmarked 54k times.

    I don’t want to analyse this character too deeply, but I think it’s the moment I realised Rockstar has really pushed the boat out here.

    According to recent reports, the sheer variety of body types, and the detail invested into them, is unprecedented really. Mandy is just one of many similarly realistic NPCs in the game.

    And while the character is almost certainly a psychopath, it’s been amusing to see her go viral overnight.

    Enjoy all the newly introduced followers, Lexie!

    Crema Games' Temtem was one of the better Pokémon-likes we had played when it arrived on Switch back in 2022. The dev released its final update a couple of years back, but soon, we'll get a chance to play its Survivors-style spinoff.

    Recent findings suggest that temtem: Swarm launches on Switch on 21st January 2027 after coming to Steam back in April. An initial glance made us think this was Crema's take on Pokémon Unite, but on closer inspection, it's far more Vampire Survivors.

    This one sees you choose your Pokémon Tem fighter and face off against swarms of corrupted creatures to survive for as long as you can. There are mini-bosses to tackle along the way, and a stream of upgrades and abilities to keep you on your toes as you progress through runs.

    Excitingly, the Switch version will launch with full cross-platform co-op, so you'll be able to team up with pals on PC or PS5 right from the jump.

    Here's a brief rundown of the game's key features and a handful of screenshots:.

    It has been revealed that team Up to Survive the Swarm: Battle relentless Tem swarms solo or with up to 3 friends in intense co-op! Strategize, share resources, and unleash overpowered synergies to defeat bosses. Booming Boss Battles: Conquer unique stages by strategizing against challenging mini-bosses and epic stage bosses. Face iconic Temtem like Gharunder, Yowlar, and Nessla in hand-crafted stages. Unleash Unstoppable Ultimates: Unleash devastating attacks, defensive abilities, or map-clearing power-ups with each Tems Ultimate ability. Master timing and unleash these incredible powers to turn the tide of battle. Evolve to Endure: Earn XP, level up your Temtem, and unlock powerful final evolutions. Each evolution grants massive boosts to skills and strength for ultimate survival. Discover All the Tems: Collect and capture every Temtem to unlock powerful Traits and unique Ultimates. Master each Temtem in solo and co-op to overcome any challenge. Revive and Thrive: No fear of defeat! Support fallen teammates in Ghost Mode until they can revive you to rejoin the fight. Online co-op ensures the adventure never ends, even after a tough encounter.

    We had a good enough time with Temtem on Switch back in 2022, and the Survivors-like spin-off is an interesting idea on the surface. A 'Mostly Positive' review streak on Steam has us hopeful that it'll be worth a look in the early days of 2027.

    Will you check out Temtem: Swarm on Switch next year? Let us know in the comments.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that "Nobody was hurt" in a shooting last week near the California office of Clockwork Revolution developers InXile, both the studio and local police have confirmed. The incident, which took place on November 11th, is right now being investigated and police have reportedly taken a suspect into custody.

    "Officers got there [on November 11th]," Tustin police sergeant Christopher Peterson stated in statement to Aftermath. "They responded to a report of a drive-by shooting there. Located multiple shell casings. Nobody was hurt. Processed the crime scene, and then sometime [Friday] morning, a little before 11 [AM], they took a suspect into custody. And the investigation is still kind of ongoing as to where and why.".

    "We’re relieved that no one was hurt at our inXile office," a spokesperson for InXile stated in a separate statement. "Our focus is on supporting our team, and we are working closely with law enforcement as they investigate.".

    Recent findings suggest that inXile are set to release steampunk RPG Clockwork Revolution next year. The studio, developers of the likes of Wasteland 3 and The Bard's Tale IV, are one of the few Xbox-owned studios not to have been affected - at least as of writing - by Microsoft's ongoing mass layoffs this year.

    Sources indicate that since being announced in 2023, Clockwork Revolution's dripped with Bioshock-ish vibes and popped up semi-regularly at Xbox showcases. "Wield the power of an incredible device to travel back in time, changing the past and rewriting the future of the city you call home: the vibrant steampunk metropolis of Avalon," reads its Steam synopsis. "In this immersive RPG, you'll step into the shoes of Morgan Vanette, a fully customizable player-character and member of the Rotten Row Hooligans. Travel between past and present as you battle the ruthless Lady Ironwood, who has been manipulating time to keep the working class struggling while amassing immense wealth and power.".

    Best wishes to the staff at InXile, here's hoping that going forwards they're able to get with making what's looking to be an intriguingly funky game without enduring any more concerning incidents like this one.

    Grand Theft Auto 6 has stunned players as well as other game developers, with Naughty Dog veteran and Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet world design director Michael Barclay praising the game with a mix of disbelief and hyperbole.

    "I've made video games for 19 years and GTA VI appears to me as a Bugatti Veyron would to a nervous Victorian child," Barclay states on Twitter. The Veyron 16.4 can reach 100km/h in 2.5 seconds, Bugatti claims, whereas a Victorian child would obviously need considerable setup time and mechanical assistance – that is, a trebuchet – to even approach such speeds.

    Barclay worked on Star Wars: Battlefront 3 at Free Radical Design, The Shoot at Cohort Studios, and also put in years at Crytek and Cloud Imperium Games before joining Naughty Dog in 2016. On his blog, he goes into great depth on the making of The Last of Us Part 2 among many other games and ideas.

    "I'm always astonished that their environmental lighting is mostly dynamic and looks as good if not better than most baked lighting," Barclay notes of Rockstar in a separate post. "They do matte style overcast lighting during cloudy days that looks so realistic I just sit and look at the street," he adds.

    In a recent development, tim Soret, head of The Last Night developer Odd Tales, agrees with Barclay. "I concur. It truly is alien technology. Hard to comprehend," he states in a post.

    GTA 6 is a top-to-bottom marvel. Our GTA 6 review calls it the highest-fidelity sandbox ever crafted, and its Metacritic score positions it as the highest-rated game of all time. Soon enough, we'll surely hear official figures from Rockstar and Take-Two enshrining it as the biggest media launch in human history. Early estimations put it at around 25 million copies and $2.36 billion grossed.

    A new report reckons 40% of developers in the video games industry are using generative AI - but even more think it's harmful

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (522 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Despite all the outrage and criticism around game developers and publishers using generative AI in gaming, a newly introduced report from the Game Developers Conference (GDC) calculates that as many as 40 percent of developers active in the industry use the controversial tools in their work.
    • That's according to the latest State of the Game Industry report from GDC, which gathers data from more than 2,300 respondents including, but not limited to, game industry professionals, made up of developers, producers, marketers, executives, and investors.
    • The report notes that 57 percent of developers who say they do use it, use gen-AI for "text generation, research, early prototyping, coding, and presentations".
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Despite all the outrage and criticism around game developers and publishers using generative AI in gaming, a newly introduced report from the Game Developers Conference (GDC) calculates that as many as 40 percent of developers active in the industry use the controversial tools in their work. This is up four percent compared to the same report last year.

    That's according to the latest State of the Game Industry report from GDC, which gathers data from more than 2,300 respondents including, but not limited to, game industry professionals, made up of developers, producers, marketers, executives, and investors.

    The report notes that 57 percent of developers who say they do use it, use gen-AI for "text generation, research, early prototyping, coding, and presentations". There appears to be a big split between triple-A studios that use gen-AI (with 27 percent of triple-A developers noting that they "feel encouraged or pressured" to use it) and indie devs, of which only nine percent say the same. Perhaps unsurprisingly - given how vocally against gen-AI a lot of 'frontline developers' have been - the tools are mostly used by "business operations and services, mobile-only studios, and free-to-play developers".

    Industry observers note that there seems to be a gap in the ages of those willing to use AI tools as well; per the report, over half (54 percent) of people 45 years or older reported using the tools - an eight-point increase from last year's survey. There is also more usage among men (45 percent) than women (33 percent).

    It has been revealed that what is perhaps more striking is that more people responded to the survey saying that they think AI is having a negative impact on games (55 percent) than responded saying they use the tech, suggesting a trend of caution rather than widespread adoption. Notably, respondents saying they are wary of the technology increased one percent since last year, so more people think AI is having a negative effect on the industry now than at the same time in 2025. Perhaps that's because of the sweeping layoffs we've seen across the games industry, often mentioned in the same breath as AI. Or the 'AI slop' that's been flooding Steam and pushing more traditional developers out. Orr some of the abysmal projects we've seen launch that have clearly used gen-AI assets.

    "I did not get into a creative industry to hand over the creativity to an algorithm," said one respondent from the UK when explaining why they don't use gen-AI tools. "I got into this industry to collaborate with creative people, not to have an advanced chatbot riff on the ideas of someone who was laid off," said another from California. "I believe that no one should have to read what no human has written and shouldn't have to see what no human has created," said yet another from Minnesota.

    The use of generative AI remains controversial in the games industry, though with big companies like Epic and Microsoft doubling down on the tech, it seems this split between developers that want to embrace it and those that don't is only growing larger.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Crimson Desert and DokeV developer Pearl Abyss is planning to further integrate generative AI into its workflow.
    • The South Korean studio said as much in its latest quarterly Earnings Letter, explaining that it had previously "validated game systems only after implementing them manually." Now, Pearl Abyss is using AI "to rapidly validate diverse design concepts prior to actual implementation," and argues the move "enables a more efficient allocation of development resources and enhances overall production speed.".

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Crimson Desert and DokeV developer Pearl Abyss is planning to further integrate generative AI into its workflow.

    The South Korean studio said as much in its latest quarterly Earnings Letter, explaining that it had previously "validated game systems only after implementing them manually." Now, Pearl Abyss is using AI "to rapidly validate diverse design concepts prior to actual implementation," and argues the move "enables a more efficient allocation of development resources and enhances overall production speed.".

    "However, AI serves strictly as a tool to support concept validation and pipeline productivity, while the core gameplay experience and actual content creation remain fully driven by our development team," the developer said.

    When Crimson Desert first introduced, players spotted a crop of suspicious in-game images that looked like they were prompted into existence. Pearl Abyss soon explained that some "2D visual props" were generated with AI tools, but were always intended to be replaced with human-made art, before rapidly patching them out of the hit open-world game.

    Industry observers note that it seems Pearl Abyss is now even more keen on the controversial tech, however: "We are integrating AI technologies to enhance development productivity and overall quality. AI is being utilized across various stages of development - including the automation of repetitive tasks, content creation support, and test optimization - and we are expanding its implementation throughout our entire development pipeline. We view AI not as a substitute for human developers, but as a tool to elevate development efficiency and quality. We will continue to expand our application of AI to deliver higher-fidelity games to the market more expeditiously.".

    Industry observers note that elsewhere in the letter, the studio noted its previously confirmed creature-collector DokeV is "targeting a launch in the second half of 2028" and we should hear more about it within the year. DokeV was initially targeting a 2023 launch a few years ago. Meanwhile, Crimson Desert is being prepped for a Nintendo Switch 2 launch "in the first half of next year.".

    It has been revealed that the use of generative AI in game development has been a hot topic for years, though it's only become more prevalent in recent months as 'AI slop' floods Steam and big companies like Epic Games proudly adopt the tech. A recent report even estimated that around 40 percent of active developers use AI tools in their work.

    HoYoverse just wrapped up a stacked Honkai: Star Rail Special Program, delivering the one-two punch of revealing the game’s next major upgrade, and detailing what you can expect from its third anniversary celebrations.

    According to recent reports, first off, Version 4.2, dubbed So Laughed the Masses, arrives April 22, making two characters playable, and bringing back a host of beloved characters for re-runs. The new update continues the Phantasmoon Games arc, as the story takes an especially suspect new development.

    It has been revealed that the big inciting incident of this latest chapter is the reveal that whoever wins the Phantasmoon Games will also become the permanent Aeon of Elation. Meanwhile, Fulwish has invited all Supplicants to the Fulwish TV HQ to announce their intention to host a TV debate about the ultimate goal of the Phantasmoon Games.

    Naturally, you’re invited, and you’ll have to overcome the challenges that await to gather more Wishpower.

    It has been revealed that our first new arrival is Silver Wolf LV.999, with whom you should already be familiar from her Version 1 form. The difference now, of course, is that she’s getting a brand-new alternate kit, since — true to her new name — she's evolved into a Godmode Player upon reaching Level 999. Silver Wolf LV.999 is a 5-Star Imaginary character on the Path of Elation.

    Her main combat trick is the ability to rack up Hidden MMR, which is what allows her to eventually activate her Cartridge and settle into the aforementioned Godmode state. While in that form, she shifts the entire battle into the virtual world, pulling in both teams into her gaming domain.

    This is essentially a world under her control, which is why she can unlock a Reward Stage at the start of her turn, which lets her spawn in-game items. When picked up, these items can turn the tide of battle.

    Keeping up with the ultra-gamer persona, Silver Wolf's Aha Instant strike blasts all enemies with a laser cannon, dealing massive damage. Perhaps her most interesting ability is being able to hack into the battlefield when she’s not actively on the team, something she can do when a teammate falls under enemy control.

    Recent findings suggest that evanescia is the other newly-playable character, who has thus far only been an observer of the Phantasmoon Games, as well as one of the most prominent new characters we've met so far on Planarcadia. V4.2 sees the girl join the roster as a 5-Star Physical character who’s likewise on the Path of Elation. As she fights, she always accumulates Certified Banger, when she earns the title she’s able to simultaneously regenerate Energy and maintain her damage.

    Evanescia’s damage continues to increase the more Certified Banger she accumulates, triggering an attack from Master Fox upon reaching a certain threshold, which deals damage to all enemies and regenerates Energy for herself. Her Elation Skill adds a bit of a performance to her kit, and is capable of hitting all enemies.

    You may have noticed the Path of Elation theme in this one, so you won’t be surprised to learn that the Elation Trailblazer variant on the main playable character is also joining the team in 4.2. There’s a new weapon that starts off as a glow stick but can transform into a lightblade as you deal damage, and, yes, gain Certified Banger.

    According to recent reports, it can also turn into nunchucks, which delivers a unique flurry of attacks on all enemies surrounding the character, dealing multiple instances of damage. You can also use it to cheer for a teammate, hyping them up.

    Recent findings suggest that version 4.2 Warp Events will bring back six characters. The first half will see reruns of The Dahlia, Castorice, and Firefly. The second half will give you another shot at unlocking Tribbie, Sunday, and Feixiao. What’s more, four of the game’s characters will be buffed in this enhancement, so you may want to reconsider putting them them back on your team. They are Firefly, Huohuo, Seele, and Welt.

    Sources indicate that as part of the same enhancement, you can expect the debut of the Cosmic Data Roaming event, which goes live alongside the anniversary celebrations. The event lets you live the life of a streamer.

    Sources indicate that currency Wars is getting a significant expansion, too. Likewise, the Cosmicon Collective is getting its version 2.0 patch, adding fresh decks, dice as well as a new team challenge game mode.

    Recent findings suggest that elsewhere, you’ll find newly introduced items in the Gift of Stardust Store, including a new outfit for Castorice. Between the time 4.2 releases and when the celebrations begin, you’ll be able to try your luck in Aha's Chosen: Spreading Elation Everywhere, an online event where you can leave a message for a chance to win various prizes.

    Marvel’s Wolverine may have started strong in September’s Circana sales report, but it plunged in October.

    Sony’s big PS5 exclusive for 2026, which attracted reasonable if utterly unremarkable reviews, ranked 14th in the latest US best-sellers list – dropping dramatically from first position the month of its release.

    According to recent reports, the game is now 15th overall for 2026 as a whole, down from 11th position in September. It’ll continue to fall with juggernauts like GTA 6 now officially out.

    The exclusive’s lore accurate lack of legs can likely be attributed to the game’s worse than expected reviews.

    While it’s not universally disliked – we awarded it an 8/10, after all – fans understandably expect better from dev Insomniac.

    Sony’s running discounts on the game during Black Friday to try and stimulate some enthusiasm around it, and I suspect this may be one of those titles that ends up in a lot of hardware bundles in the future.

    To be fair, the platform holder seemed relatively satisfied with the title’s 2.4 million sales during its recent financial report.

    I suppose it’s possible the launch numbers really did meet its expectations, but it may now be disappointed with the title’s long-term momentum – or lack thereof.

    We’ll probably have to wait until its next investor revision before we get more information.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that we've been keeping an eye out for news of Nintendo's playable and electric ocarinas going on sale in Europe for a good while now. It looks like sales are just around the corner, but you're going to need to jump through some hoops if you want to get your hands on one.

    Industry observers note that both the Nintendo playable model and HORI electric version will initially be sold on an invite-only basis in Europe. You can register your interest in getting either model now on the Nintendo website, but there are some criteria that you'll have to pass first.

    It has been revealed that firstly, you'll need to have a Nintendo account registered in Europe (excluding Norway, Russia and South Africa), have allowed Nintendo to process your usage information to customise services, offers and recommendations in your Nintendo Account settings, and have allowed Nintendo to send email recommendations about games, events, special offers and more. You'll need to have done all of that by 22nd November.

    You can only register your interest if you have "reached at least 10 hours of play time in the Nintendo Switch 2 game The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time by 18/11/2026" using the same Nintendo account you use to register.

    Sources indicate that and that's just to get an invite. On the day that the products become available, those who are invited will receive an email with a link to purchase either ocarina (limited to one each per customer).

    The playable ocarina will set you back £29.99, bundling the instrument with a wrist strap and sheet music for all of the in-game songs. HORI's electric option is a little more expensive at £41.99, but also comes with a dedicated stand.

    Have you registered your interest for either model? Let us know in the comments.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • A hacker has pleaded guilty to a number of online crimes, including the 2022 breach of Rockstar Games which resulted in a bunch of mid-development clips of GTA 6 in action leaking onto the net.
    • In a recent development, the BBC report that, on November 16th, Arion Kurtaj pleaded guilty at Woolwich Crown Court to the Rockstar Games hack and a number of others he carried out with the hacking gang Lapsus$ while aged 16 and 17.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    A hacker has pleaded guilty to a number of online crimes, including the 2022 breach of Rockstar Games which resulted in a bunch of mid-development clips of GTA 6 in action leaking onto the net.

    In a recent development, the BBC report that, on November 16th, Arion Kurtaj pleaded guilty at Woolwich Crown Court to the Rockstar Games hack and a number of others he carried out with the hacking gang Lapsus$ while aged 16 and 17. Kurtaj, now aged 21, was previously sentenced to stay in a secure hospital indefinitely due to the severity of his autism, but was subsequently deemed fit to stand trial. He'll be sentenced at a later date.

    It has been revealed that kurtaj carried out the 2022 Rockstar hack while on bail for other hacking offences and being housed at a Travelodge hotel under police protection, the latter on account of rival hackers threatening to attack him over stolen Bitcoin stashes. The Rockstar hack was reportedly done using an Amazon Fire Stick plugged into the hotel room's TV, plus a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse.

    90 clips of unfinished GTA 6 were flung online by that hack, with Rockstar having refused to cooperate with Kurtaj's demand via an internal Slack channel that the company contact him on massaging app Telegram within 24 hours. Rockstar claimed the breach cost them $5m million to recover from, in addition to staff having to waste thousands of hours.

    Earlier this year, GTA 6 suffered yet another leak, with a hacker or hackers going by "Cyberleek" posting various videos of the game in action. Rockstar and parent organization Take-Two promptly sprung into action, taking down videos, filing subpoenas, and issuing a statement that called the leak "heartbreaking".

    It has been revealed that hopefully with the game's console release later this week, those will be the only two GTA 6 leaks which have to be added to the annals of gaming history. As much as marketing can leave a bad taste in the mouth, especially when it barely shows anything of the actual product being advertised, neither of the GTA 6 leaks served much of a purpose beyond forcing people to waste some time and energy talking about the perpetrators.

    The Legend of Zelda was in "dire straits" before Breath of the Wild gave the beloved series a massive second wind, according to two former Nintendo marketing leads.

    The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time's most recent remake has been a mega success, becoming the fastest-selling Switch 2 game so far, but the shiny latest adventure has also prompted some online debate over where the series should go next. Should Zelda lean into its carefully directed history - like the one brilliantly remade in Ocarina of Time - or keep the ball rolling with Breath of the Wild's wide open, spontaneous sandbox?

    Nintendo of America's ex-director of social media marketing Kit Ellis and former public relations manager Krysta Yang chimed in on the discourse in their latest podcast (below), and explained that Zelda wasn't doing too hot before the Switch era.

    "There has been some revisionist history out there lately," Ellis noted in response to fans who reckon "the Zelda team ripped away" series staples, like classic dungeons and linear worlds, at the height of their popularity.

    In a recent development, "I remember, I was going to the focus groups where it was a really dark moment," Ellis continued. "The feedback was like, 'The fan base is dwindling. This is not bringing in latest players.'".

    The Legend of Zelda was supposedly "shrinking," while "interest in the audience was getting smaller and smaller" with each upcoming entry. "They had to do something dramatic," Ellis said.

    "This series was in dire straits. They were selling, like, nothing," Yang added.

    The Zelda series was certainly never irrelevant, but there's a pretty big gap between the roughly 8m copies Twilight Princess sold at the beginning of the Wii generation, the roughly 3m copies Skyward Sword sold at the end of the console's life, and the 34m copies that Breath of the Wild sold just one console generation later.

    Industry observers note that it was a success so substantial it spawned a wildly ambitious sequel, Tears of the Kingdom, and even influenced the latest 2D Zelda, Echoes of Wisdom. Now that classic Zelda's back in the spotlight, though, I do hope Nintendo's able to slot the series' curated dungeons into whatever the next mainline game becomes.

    #51899. Metro 2039 goes back to its Metro underground roots, with a story shaped by the war in Ukraine and the people who suffer it

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Vg247 ↗ Open Full Page

    Metro 2039 goes back to its Metro underground roots, with a story shaped by the war in Ukraine and the people who suffer it

    📅 16 Apr 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (443 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Vg247

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, the Metro series is finally, officially back with a new installment.
    • Recent findings suggest that 2039 takes an unusual route with its scope, however.
    • What won’t be changing is the kind of game that it is.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, the Metro series is finally, officially back with a new installment. 4A Games has just unveiled Metro 2039 to the world, the follow-up to the outstanding Metro Exodus, released all the way back in 2019.

    Recent findings suggest that 2039 takes an unusual route with its scope, however. Rather than build on the semi-open-world structure of Exodus, the upcoming sequel instead brings the focus back to where it all began: the Metro.

    What won’t be changing is the kind of game that it is. Metro 2039 remains, like its predecessors, a story-driven, single-player game. Returning to the confined spaces of the Moscow Metro brings the focus back to the claustrophobic, uneasy atmosphere of the original games.

    The game’s protagonist is, for the first time, going to be voiced throughout. From what we’ve been able to see, the psychological horror in this installment will be driven more by the very real effects the apocalypse has had, and continues to have, on denizens of the Metro.

    2039 has been in development for years, but 4A Games has been rocked by two considerable events: the 2020 Covid pandemic, and Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine, where the developer is based. The game’s darker story has changed in response to that.

    The team’s Ukrainian perspective is molded into the narrative, and more prominently represents the toll the events of the last several years has taken on members of the team, their families and communities.

    According to the developer, you can expect a bigger emphasis on choice and consequence, with Russian author Dmitry Glukhovsky returning to co-write a narrative that explores the compromised morality of a post-war society.

    The new protagonist’s return to the Metro comes with the reveal that the different underground factions are now united under one banner, the not-so-subtly named Novoreich. Lead by a former Spartan, the Novoreich is an authoritarian regime which offers what it believes to be the only path to salvation.

    Recent findings suggest that 4A Games remains majority Ukrainian, with teams based in Kyiv, and Malta. Unlike most AAA projects today, the studio continues to rely on its own engine tech. The 4A Engine is given a major upgrade for 2039: ray tracing is now a core component of the rendering pipeline, but the tech has been rebuilt to run better on modern hardware.

    Today’s reveal sadly didn’t feature much gameplay - only a brief first-look with a mix of gameplay and cinematics. The developer, however, emphasised that creating cluttered, believable and lived-in environments remains a key focus.

    Metro 2039 is set for release sometime this winter on PC, Xbox Series X/S, and PS5.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    UPDATE 17TH NOVEMBER: The Blood of Dawnwalker update 1.2 - the update that brings a New Game Plus mode, predominantly - is now available on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series S/X.

    It has been revealed that new Game Plus, as mentioned below, raises the level cap to 100, and scales enemies and regions in the game around you. Previously, the game was zone-scaled, so some zones were tougher than others. In New Game Plus, this will no longer be the case, so you can go and explore Xanthe's region at the back of Vale Sangora straight away, if you want to.

    In a recent development, there'll be fresh versions of equipment with new stats to find, and they'll be labelled with "NG+" so you know when you've picked one up. You can unlock New Game Plus from the main menu after choosing your base save and difficulty option. All of your accrued skill perks and abilities will be available to you at the start of the Withering Away quest in the game's prologue.

    The full patch notes for Dawnwalker revision 1.2 are:.

    ORIGINAL STORY 13TH NOVEMBER: A New Game Plus mode is coming to vampiric RPG The Blood of Dawnwalker next week.

    Developer Rebel Wolves has now detailed everything coming with The Blood of Dawnwalker's Enhancement 1.2, presently planned to go live sometime next week, and top of the list of changes is a New Game Plus for players who have already rolled credits on the game.

    According to recent reports, "If you completed the Epilogue, you can dive right back into Vale Sangora with New Game+," the developer revealed earlier today. "Your level, skills, and inventory will carry over." Rebel Wolves is upping the level cap to 100 for New Game Plus, which will also have items with updated stats and enemies "balanced and scaled uniformly across all regions.".

    Elsewhere in Upgrade 1.2, the studio is making tweaks to "enemy health pools and how often they use their abilities during combat," and improving terrain geometry to allow for "smoother movement during combat and exploration." We'll need to wait for more comprehensive patch notes before finding out which enemies are getting spongier or flimsier, however.

    While the incoming patch doesn't seem to be as beefy as the last - the one that added animal petting and an easier Story mode - it'll be a good way to sink your teeth deeper into a game that's already begging to be replayed, thanks to a time management mechanic that can drastically change any given run.

    Industry observers note that the new game from some former The Witcher 3 veterans came out in September and seems to have been a hit. Eurogamer's The Blood of Dawnwalker review called the game a "familiar dark fantasy adventure, but one with bold and provocative ideas of its own, that's mostly, enormously successful.".

    Sources indicate that tech giant Intel are being taken to court for allegedly "misleading" their investors about the sheer scale of the impact of generative AI-fuelled component price hikes on PC sales. The class action lawsuit in question claims that Intel's distribution and manufacturing partners have had to deal with "a massive glut of unwanted PC inventory", and that the gains from Intel's investments in AI datacenters aren't enough to make up for slowing sales of PCs to regular Josephines who just want fancy boxes they can play Deadlock on.

    All this follows Intel's last round of quarterly results, in which they unveiled a significant revenue fall; this triggered an Intel stock price drop from $92.07 per share on October 29th to $65.76 per share the next day, which this week's lawsuit characterises as "the largest single-day price decline for Intel common stock in over 50 years".

    It has been revealed that the lawyers in question are from Robbins LLP, who specialise in "shareholder, whistleblower, antitrust, & consumer litigation". In a press release, they say they've filed suit on behalf of anybody who bought Intel stock from July 23rd to October 29th this year.

    The suit claims that Intel neglected to tell investors that falling PC and component sales were having a "materially greater negative impact" on their third financial quarter 2026 Client Computing and Physical AI Groupresults than Intel had previously stated – to the tune of "hundreds of millions of dollars" in revenue shrinkage, compared to the previous quarter, with the situation still expected to "worsen".

    They also accuse the organization of keeping schtum about the aforesaid "massive glut of unwanted PC inventory", together with the fact that "any positive impacts to Intel’s business and financial results resulting from data center construction and other aspects of the AI boom were more than offset by the negative effects on the Company’s business and financial results resulting from the PC market slowdown and the excess inventory buildup described above.".

    Sources indicate that finally, they say Intel bosses have failed to disclose that they're struggling to procure an adequate supply of substrates – that is, materials used to create the base layer of chips, circuit boards and similar components. As such, the lawyers claim, Intel couldn't "ramp up production to meet data center CPU demand even if the Company chose to divert production resources because of a slowdown in PC-related sales.".

    Once the Godzilla of personal computing, Intel haven't been having a brilliant few years. Back in 2024, they recorded a multi-billion dollar quarterly loss, pushing then-CEO Pat Gelsinger to resign. As regards sales of gaming PCs, they've fallen behind AMD, though they've reportedly taken some ground back recently as regards desktop CPUs. As regards graphics cards, they have long been dwarfed by Nvidia.

    Sources indicate that netflix first announced a Magic: The Gathering series in June 2019, with Avengers: Endgame directors Joe and Anthony Russo attached, and it was originally due in late 2022.     ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that the Sims 4 players on PlayStation and Xbox have now caught up to their friends on PC, at least when it comes to the game’s Marketplace.
    • As often happens when long-established games introduce paid mods, The Sims 4’s wasn’t especially well-received, in part because of the introduction of a new premium currency - Moola - that is the only way to purchase any of that content.
    • The Moola denominations and prices are similar to many other in-game currencies, and the criticism around them is the same: they obfuscate the true value of items, and because of the way those denominations are structured, you’ll never be able to buy exactly what you need.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that the Sims 4 players on PlayStation and Xbox have now caught up to their friends on PC, at least when it comes to the game’s Marketplace. This latest feature is essentially a hub for paid mods and other user-created content.

    As often happens when long-established games introduce paid mods, The Sims 4’s wasn’t especially well-received, in part because of the introduction of a new premium currency - Moola - that is the only way to purchase any of that content.

    The Moola denominations and prices are similar to many other in-game currencies, and the criticism around them is the same: they obfuscate the true value of items, and because of the way those denominations are structured, you’ll never be able to buy exactly what you need.

    Industry observers note that for most games, the subject of paid mods has always been fraught, and that's certainly true for The Sims 4. In the announcement blog post, Maxis remarked that the launch on consoles will work similarly to what PC players have seen, in that Kits will no longer be available to buy directly with real money on the PlayStation and Microsoft Stores. While Expansion Packs, Game Packs, and Stuff Packs will remain, you’ll need to buy Moola if you want to acquire Kits going forward.

    Interestingly, however, EA seems to have changed its mind somewhat on the Kits situation. A recently leaked memo (via SimsCommunity), appears to show that the publisher intends on making Kits available for purchase directly again, without the need for Moola.

    Industry observers note that unfortunately, this only appears to affect the PC version, with the reversion reportedly forthcoming on both the EA App as well as Steam. Indeed, according to the same report, the change has already taken place on the former, with the latter following on April 20.

    Considering the Marketplace only just launched on consoles, the company may wait to see if the decision to remove Kits from console platform marketplaces will be as poorly received as it has been on PC.

    If you’re looking to jump back into The Sims 4 to check out all the new paid content, make sure you’re well-equipped with our list of Sims 4 cheats and debug options, or this one specifically for the Royalty & Legacy expansion cheats.

    Avoiding Steam Machine this Black Friday? Here's what other mini PCs can actually get you for your cash

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1612 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamesradar

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Steam Machine is now "checkout-ready" according to Valve, but with a $1,049 starting price for the 512GB base model (and that $1,349 rate on the 2TB version up for debate in the near-future), there's a problem for those who don't want to break four figures on a upcoming system.
    • That's where the well-established (but recently far more popular) world of mini PCs comes in.
    • These devices have been finding themselves in more homes this year, as increased prices of the best gaming PCs and even cheaper components have pushed both those after a productivity and gaming solution towards more budget-friendly alternatives.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Steam Machine is now "checkout-ready" according to Valve, but with a $1,049 starting price for the 512GB base model (and that $1,349 rate on the 2TB version up for debate in the near-future), there's a problem for those who don't want to break four figures on a upcoming system.

    That's where the well-established (but recently far more popular) world of mini PCs comes in. Whether you want more options further down the price range or you're after something with more graphical grunt, these compact PCs prove it's not just Valve producing ready-to-go gaming machines that don't take up floor space.

    These devices have been finding themselves in more homes this year, as increased prices of the best gaming PCs and even cheaper components have pushed both those after a productivity and gaming solution towards more budget-friendly alternatives.

    In a recent development, I've spent the last few months road-testing mini PCs from Geekom to Asus, spanning the full price range. Right at the bottom, boxes like the $499 Geekom A5 2027 Edition will gear themselves heavily towards indie titles and retro emulation. At the top, you'll find full dedicated GPU options spanning up to the RTX 5070.

    It's worth noting that the Windows operating system won't give you that living-room-console ease of the Steam Machine, but instead opens you up to more versatility around launchers and OS compatibility.

    Like you, I was curious to see what these tiny little rigs could actually conjure - and you'll find out exactly how each price point fared in my benchmarks just below.

    Recent findings suggest that I've spent the last six months running my everyday workflow through mini PCs across a range of brands, testing every compact rig I can get my hands on in whatever games they allow for. Around that, I've also been testing and reviewing gaming laptops on GamesRadar+ for the last six years, using similar components in different configurations every two weeks.

    The best deal you'll find on the budget Geekom A5 2027 Edition right now sits with Amazon. A $50 discount on the original $549 takes us to $499 this Black Friday. While prices have been jumping since the start of the year here, that's cheaper than it has been since July. This one's dropped to around $400 earlier in 2026, though.

    The Geekom A5 2027 Edition is a productivity machine first and foremost. The AMD Ryzen 7 7730U under the hood is designed to run efficiently, quietly, and with minimal power draw. That means it can hum away in the background without breaking the bank, but it also sweeps away a lot of the power more demanding games require.

    Industry observers note that I was still curious to see how gaming actually fares at the lower end of the budget. In short, this thing will run your indie Steam library no problem. If you prioritize smaller titles, you'll get on just fine here and likely kick yourself if you opt for anything more expensive. Retro emulation runs nicely as well, if that's your jam.

    Sources indicate that that's about as far as you'll get, though. Shadow of the Tomb Raider, an older "double-A" release that doesn't tend to make too many gaming laptops sweat, neared smooth framerates only with resolution set to 720p and settings dropped to their lowest. Medium can just about squeak by on a smaller screen at 28fps.

    In a recent development, the same story is true of Cyberpunk 2077, the big guns test. Without frame generation you're looking at 27fps at 720p here, though we do jump up nicely to 45fps with a little extra help.

    Recent findings suggest that these more demanding games are playable. They run. You can even get over 30fps if you make larger sacrifices - a perfectly decent position at the budget end of the spectrum. They're just not going to feel nearly as good as they might slightly further up the price scale.

    Sources indicate that the GMKTec K8 Plus has dropped under $700 in the past, but today's $170 discount is a starting point. I'd keep a close eye on this one as Black Friday progresses, rather than diving in straight away now - this one stands to wriggle under that $700 threshold if we're lucky.

    The GMKTec K8 Plus upgrades your processor to the Ryzen 7 8845HS, adds an Oculink connection for future eGPU upgrades, and includes extra support for more monitor displays. That's a set of upgrades that will set you up for more demanding games a lot better than the budget-minded Geekom A5.

    In practice, that means solid 40+fps in Shadow of the Tomb Raider at both medium and high settings in 1080p, with Cyberpunk 2077 managing 41fps in medium as well. You've got a lot more breathing room here, as well as power ceiling that allows for that FHD resolution.

    Mid-range "double-As" are more-than possible with a few tweaks, and more demanding titles are within reach here as well.

    According to recent reports, ultimately, this is your all-rounder. It's powerful enough to represent solid value for money across chunkier games while still giving you room to grow with that eGPU connection and easily upgradeable innards.

    Industry observers note that I have one major caveat from my testing, though. You might need to upgrade the Wi-Fi card when you buy it. Internet was incredibly slow for me during testing, far slower than any other device on my network. There's something funky going on behind the scenes here, but customers have reported a fresh card solves the problem.

    The Geekom A9 Max is available with that Ryzen Ai 9 HX470 chipset, 2TB SSD and 32GB RAM for $1,499. Again this one has been cheaper this year so far, so it's worth watching over the next week. Still, it's been locked in at $1600 since August.

    According to recent reports, the Geekom A9 Max is a step up in price compared to our more budget-friendly alternatives, and overtakes the 2TB Steam Machine cost. So what's in it for you?

    Industry observers note that this is actually a very similar value proposition to the Steam Machine, hitting 30+fps in Cyberpunk 2077 at 1440p Medium settings without any frame generation help. Adding frame-gen into the equation, and it's easy to speed well past that 60fps threshold. It's a step up where more demanding games like CD Projekt Red's open world are concerned, though improvements further down the scale are more measured compared to the GMKTec further up.

    What's going to separate these two rigs, though, is what else you want to do with your PC. The Geekom A9 Max can match the Steam Machine in overall performance, but it also adds a whole workstation into your purchase.

    In a recent development, this is where Windows plays its most important card in this trip into mini PC land. While you won't have that console-like operating system, you'll have everything you need for demanding productivity tasks and workflows on top of that gaming performance. It's the better option for those not just buying a gaming device, but rolling their purchase in with their work machine.

    It has been revealed that we're down to a brand-latest record-low price on the RTX 5070 Asus ROG GR70 mini PC this Black Friday, with the $2,599 configuration shedding $300 from the final price. This one's only ever dipped just below $2,500 in previous sales, though it's still one of the most expensive mini PCs on the market.

    Sources indicate that the largest, and most expensive, mini PC I've had on my test bench so far, the Asus ROG GR70 isn't a budget alternative to the Steam Machine but an additional investment in more demanding PC games. This is a full system, with a dedicated RTX 5070 graphics card humming away inside, and some of AMD's most powerful processors up top as well.

    Sources indicate that I tested the AMD Ryzen 9 9955HX3D / RTX 5070 version with a whopping 64GB RAM under the hood. That's a particularly expensive configuration in today's rates, one that comes in at around $2,800.

    For that kind of cash, you can easily pick up one of the best gaming laptops or a cheaper full-tower PC - so the ROG GR70 is only for those specifically seeking a miniature form factor.

    How did it go? Unsurprisingly, for a rig often twice the price of the Steam Machine, pretty damn smoothly. Triple-figure frame rates are the norm for most Triple-As in high settings at FHD, while we're still well above 60fps in everything at 1440p as well.

    That's performance that's going to blow the Steam Machine out the water, but it's still tracking behind other RTX 5070 counterparts. The value of this beast compared to an RTX 5070 gaming laptop or desktop PC doesn't quite stack up - you'll need to know you're in it for the miniature footprint for this premium pick to make sense.

    We're also rounding up the best gaming handhelds and best gaming tablets for more ways to play this holiday season.

    Sources indicate that managing Editor of Hardware at GamesRadar+, I originally landed in hardware at our sister site TechRadar before moving over to GamesRadar. In between, I've written for Tom’s Guide, Wireframe, The Indie Game Website and That Video Game Blog, covering everything from the PS5 launch to the Apple Pencil. Now, i'm focused on Nintendo Switch, gaming laptops (and the keyboards, headsets and mice that come with them), PS5, and trying to find the perfect projector.

    • The Call of Duty Endowment is marking Remembrance Day and its 17th anniversary by encouraging Modern Warfare 4 and Warzone players to pick up its Valor Pack, with all of Activision's net proceeds going towards helping veterans find jobs.
